## Method and reproduction

The benchmark uses deterministic data with outliers, NaN/infinities, `sigma=3`,
`maxiters=5`, `ddof=0`, and no rollback. Mean/std and median/MAD use matching
rejection and dispersion centers. An independent NumPy reference checks masks,
fused values, diagnostic fields, and flags before timing.
Reference computations are excluded from timings.

Use the environment setup above, then run:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python benchmarks/benchmark_sigma_clip.py --repeats 15 --warmups 3 --inner 100 --csv sigma-python.csv
```

The script uses the same `_benchutils.timeit` helper as the 1-D and axis
benchmarks: 100 calls per sample, 3 warmups, and 15 samples, discarding the
lowest/highest sample before taking the median. These are absolute timings,
not a comparison with an earlier implementation or a no-regression guarantee.
The benchmark covers common configurations, not every clipping policy.

## Why it is fast

- A caller-owned Rust `Workspace` reuses masks, indices, and statistical scratch.
- Stack processing reuses column scratch within each Rayon job; callers of the
  Rust kernel control parallel scheduling.
- Fused outputs reuse valid statistics and retained-value scratch when possible.
- Python normalizes dtype and contiguity once; matching masks avoid extra reshapes.

NaN/infinities are excluded. Threshold equality survives; centers and MAD narrow
to input dtype. Mean-centered variance uses the unrounded mean; final clipped
means sum retained values sequentially in float64. Extreme residual squares or
limits can overflow, and tiny squares can underflow. These timings do not claim
to improve those numerical limits.
